explanations.answer: How can a sinful man perform such signs
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker! Others say, “How can a sinful man perform such signs?” That's a sharp question, because it points at what Jesus actually did. The Pharisees are split, and it all starts with a Sabbath and some mud.

explanations.answer: Why would God heal on that day
explanations.explanation: That sounds like it could be in there, but it isn't. The text has the other Pharisees ask, “How can a sinful man perform such signs?” They look at the sign itself and ask how someone sinful could do it. Nobody in the passage asks why God would heal on that day.

explanations.answer: Who gave this man His authority
explanations.explanation: Good question, but nobody asks it here. These Pharisees ask, “How can a sinful man perform such signs?” Their question is about the signs, not about authority. And the text says there was division among them.

explanations.answer: They are afraid of the Jews
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The text says, “His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews.” The Jews had already decided that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue. It's a pressure moment, and I think anybody who's felt that knot in their stomach understands.

explanations.answer: They are angry with their son
explanations.explanation: The text never says they're angry with him. It says they spoke up this way because they were afraid of the Jews. Their words are “Ask him. He is old enough to speak for himself.” That's fear talking, not anger.

The text gives a different reason. It says, “His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews.” Nothing says they were trying to shield Jesus. They were looking at what could happen to them.

explanations.answer: They would be put out of the synagogue
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. John 9:22 says the Jews “…had already determined that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.” Verse 23 says that was why his parents said, “He is old enough. Ask him.” That's the pressure they were under.

explanations.answer: They would be sent out of the city
explanations.explanation: That sounds serious, but it's not what the text says. John 9:22 says anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue. The threat was about the synagogue, not the city.

explanations.answer: They would have to pay a fine
explanations.explanation: No fine is mentioned, friend. John 9:22 says the Jews decided anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue. Money doesn't come into it at all.

explanations.answer: I was blind but now I see
explanations.explanation: That's the line, baker! He says, “Whether He is a sinner I do not know. There is one thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see!” He doesn't pretend to know more than he does. He stands on what he knows, and nobody can argue him off it.
He doesn't say that here. He says, “Whether He is a sinner I do not know.” What he does say he knows for sure is, “I was blind, but now I see!” He sticks to what he's lived.

explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. He says, “Who is He, Sir? Tell me so that I may believe in Him.” He's ready to believe, he just needs to know who. It's an honest question, and it gets an answer.
